walkthroughs.body_html:
Religion, Philosophy & Ethics: Relationships & Families — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Religion, Philosophy & Ethics: Relationships & Families brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Religion, Philosophy & Ethics: Relationships & Families.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which encyclical banned Catholic contraception in 1968?
options: Humanae Vitae
Rerum Novarum
Pacem in Terris
Laudato Si

mcqs.q: What is the maximum number of wives in Islam?
What does utilitarianism say is right action?
options: Jihad is the Islamic word for prayer.
Whatever makes you personally happy is the right thing to do.
The action that produces the greatest happiness for the greatest number — judged by consequences, not intentions or rules.
Utilitarianism says you should always tell the truth.

mcqs.q: What does the term jihad mean in Islam?
options: Jihad is the Islamic word for prayer.
Jihad means 'holy war' against non-Muslims.
Substance dualism means men and women are different.
Struggle or striving — the greater jihad is the internal spiritual struggle against sin; the lesser jihad refers to defensive military struggle under strict conditions.

mcqs.q: What is substance dualism about mind and body?
options: Substance dualism means men and women are different.
Substance dualism is the belief that humans have two personalities.
The view (associated with Descartes) that mind and body are two distinct kinds of substance — a non-physical mind interacting with a physical body.
Utilitarianism says you should always tell the truth.
